land.text: Anatolia and Eastern Thrace, the last Ottoman shape: 'On 1 November 1922, the Turkish Parliament in Ankara formally abolished the Sultanate'

predecessors.note: The ottoman-empire dossier ends in November 1922 and names this state as successor; Cliopatria's Republic of Turkey row starts in 1924 and its Ottoman row runs to 1923. The Grand National Assembly government of 23 April 1920 has no row of its own.

capitals.name: Ankara
capitals.note: 'officially proclaimed on 29 October 1923 in Ankara, the country's new capital'.

correction.text: the 1924 shape carried back to the proclamation of 29 October 1923

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: Cliopatria's Republic of Turkey row starts in 1924 and its Ottoman row ends in 1923, but the page has 'The Republic was proclaimed on 29 October 1923' and the Treaty of Lausanne signed on 24 July 1923 (effective 6 August 1924) gave 'international recognition of the sovereignty of the new Turkish state'. The ottoman-empire dossier ends in November 1922, so 1923 would otherwise be undrawn.

1924-1935, 763,251 km2, about 20,000 km2 under the infobox 783,562 km2 (ratio 0.97, the infobox counts Hatay and the modern state). The shape is Anatolia and Eastern Thrace without Hatay and without Mosul: Lausanne 'settled the boundaries' with Syria and Iraq 'along with the Treaty of Ankara', left 'the fate of the province of Mosul ... to be determined through the League of Nations', and Greece agreed to cede Karaagac.

1936-1938, 763,326 km2: two cells moved against 1924 (29.7 E, 41.1 N out; 26.5-26.9 E, 40.4 N in), read as noise. The Straits convention of Lausanne 'lasted for thirteen years' and was replaced by the Montreux Convention in 1936, which moved no border.

1939-1944, 768,279 km2: 19 cells (17 in Turkey, 2 in Syria, about 4,750 km2) added: the Sanjak of Alexandretta. 'By 23 July 1939, the last vestiges of the French Mandate authorities had left Antakya, and the territory was fully annexed by Turkey'; the vote was on 29 June 1939. Infobox ratio 768,279 / 783,562 = 0.98.
1945, 768,253 km2: three cells swapped on the Iranian and Armenian edges against 1939 (read as noise). The page: Turkey 'entered the war on the side of the Allies on 23 February 1945'; no territory.
1946, 768,276 km2: one Thracian edge cell (26.45 E, 41.67 N, by Edirne and Karaagac) is dropped for the year and returns in 1949; read as noise.
1947, 768,227 km2: an Armenian edge cell traded for an Iranian one against 1946; noise.
1948, 768,084 km2: one Turkish cell (26.4 E, 41.1 N) less; noise.

1949-2005, 768,204 km2, the stable outline: two cells (the Edirne edge) back after 1948. Infobox 783,562 km2 against 768,204 gives 0.98. The page: 'Turkey joined NATO in 1952' and the coups of 1960, 1971, 1980 and 1997; no territory.
2006-2013, 768,006 km2: one cell on the south-eastern edge (44.07 E, 37.31 N) dropped; noise.

2014-2023, 767,585 km2: two cells on the Syrian edge (36.3-38.7 E, 36.0-36.8 N) out and the south-eastern cell back; noise. The shape does not include the Syrian land Turkey has occupied since 24 August 2016 ('Areas of the Syrian Interim Government under military occupation (2016-2025)'), which is drawn by the occupation events, nor northern Cyprus.
2024, 767,585 km2, the 2014 outline; same remarks on the occupied zones in Syria and Cyprus.

region.text: Anatolia and Eastern Thrace: 'The Republic was proclaimed on 29 October 1923'

ledger.note: 29 October 1923: Atatürk proclaims the Republic of Turkey at Ankara. 'officially proclaimed on 29 October 1923 in Ankara, the country's new capital'; 'Mustafa Kemal became the republic's first president'. The sultanate fell on 1 November 1922 and the Treaty of Lausanne was signed on 24 July 1923. The page names no land; the Cliopatria outline is the researcher's reading.

region.text: Karaagac, across the Maritsa from Edirne

ledger.note: 6 August 1924: Lausanne takes effect and Karaagac is Turkish. 'Greece agreed to cede Karaagac to Turkey'; 'The Treaty of Lausanne became effective on 6 August 1924'. The page gives no date for the handover and the area is under one map cell, so the year is the treaty's and the land the page's.

region.text: the Sanjak of Alexandretta, the Hatay State

ledger.note: 23 July 1939: Turkey annexes Hatay. 'On 29 June 1939, following a referendum, the Hatay legislature voted to disestablish the Hatay State and join Turkey'; the Turkish Grand National Assembly passed the law on 7 July; 'By 23 July 1939 ... the territory was fully annexed by Turkey'. The referendum has been called 'phoney' and 'rigged'.

region.text: the northern part of Cyprus, 'the Turkish occupation of 37% of Cyprus' (infobox: 'Turkey occupies 36.2% of Cyprus')

ledger.note: 20 July 1974: Turkey invades Cyprus. 'Turkey invaded Cyprus on Saturday, 20 July 1974'; Turkish forces 'captured 3% of the island before a ceasefire' obtained by the UN on 22 July.

region.text: the northern part of Cyprus, 'the Turkish occupation of 37% of Cyprus' (infobox: 'Turkey occupies 36.2% of Cyprus')

ledger.note: August 1974: the second operation ends in the Turkish zone. 'On 14 August Turkey launched its Second Peace Operation', ending in 'the Turkish occupation of 37% of Cyprus'; the page records UN Security Council Resolution 360 on 16 August 1974 and no day for the end of the fighting.

region.text: the northern part of Cyprus, 'the Turkish occupation of 37% of Cyprus' (infobox: 'Turkey occupies 36.2% of Cyprus')

ledger.note: 1974: Turkey holds northern Cyprus. Infobox: 'Turkey occupies 36.2% of Cyprus'; the line is 'commonly referred to as the Green Line'. The occupation continues to 2024: Turkey is the only state that recognises the Turkish Republic of Northern Cyprus.

region.text: the Turkish Cypriot state declared on 13 February 1975 as a 'Federated Turkish State' and independent as the Turkish Republic of Northern Cyprus in 1983

ledger.note: 13 February 1975: Turkey declares the occupied area a 'Federated Turkish State', the forerunner of the Turkish Republic of Northern Cyprus (independence declared in 1983, 'Turkey is the only country that recognises it'). The relation runs to 2024.

region.text: the Euphrates Shield area, 2,225 km2, 'towns such as Al-Bab, Azaz, ... Jarabulus, Rajo' (circles around Jarabulus and al-Bab, no place name in the gazetteer)

ledger.note: 24 August 2016: Turkey enters northern Syria. Operation Euphrates Shield, 'First offensive: 24 August 2016'; 'The Syrian National Army captured an area of 2,225 square kilometres'. The infobox calls the zones 'under military occupation (2016-2025)'.

region.text: 'the entire Afrin District' (circle around Afrin, no place name in the gazetteer)

ledger.note: 20 January 2018: Operation Olive Branch takes Afrin. 'Second offensive: 20 January 2018'; 'the capture of the entire Afrin District'. The page gives no end date for the operation.

region.text: the Peace Spring area, 3,412-4,220 km2, '68 settlements, including Ras al-Ayn, Tell Abyad, Suluk, Mabrouka and Manajir' (circles around Tell Abyad and Ras al-Ayn)

ledger.note: 9 October 2019: Operation Peace Spring. 'Third offensive: 9 October 2019'; 'a total area of between 3,412 square kilometres and 4,220 square kilometres' with '68 settlements, including Ras al-Ayn, Tell Abyad'.

zones.text: the northern part of Cyprus, 'the Turkish occupation of 37% of Cyprus' (infobox: 'Turkey occupies 36.2% of Cyprus')

wars.outcome: Turkish victory: Turkish forces took about 36-37% of the island in two operations (20 July and 14 August 1974) and have occupied it since; the Turkish Cypriot state was declared on 13 February 1975 and again in 1983.
wars.note: The page gives the ceasefire as 22 July 1974, not 16 August; it records Resolution 360 on 16 August.

'the entire Afrin District' (circle around Afrin, no place name in the gazetteer)

wars.outcome: Turkey and the Syrian National Army hold the Euphrates Shield (2,225 km2), Afrin (2018) and Peace Spring (3,412-4,220 km2) zones as occupied land; the infobox runs the occupation to 2025.
wars.note: Operation Spring Shield began on 27 February 2020 in Idlib; the page gives no boundary for it. The page does not name the other fighting parties in the text returned, so only the Syrian state and the Turkish-backed army are listed.

certainty.note: The Treaty of Lausanne was signed on 24 July 1923 but took effect on 6 August 1924; the Mosul frontier was still open.

Frontiers fixed by the 1921 Ankara agreement and Lausanne, and the 1939 Hatay annexation; the Turkish-Iraqi frontier of Mosul was left to the League of Nations and was not read. The line in Cyprus (the Green Line) is a ceasefire line and the occupied zones in northern Syria (2016-2024) have no fixed boundary.

notes:
Cliopatria's Republic of Turkey row is one outline for a century (2,784 to 2,803 cells) with one real change, Hatay in 1939; all other differences are edge cells of 1-3 cells. Start: the page gives 29 October 1923 while the Ottoman dossier ends in November 1922 and Cliopatria starts the Republic in 1924, so a keyframe for 1923 was added. The Grand National Assembly government of 1920-1923 and the War of Independence (19 May 1919 on the page's infobox) predate the dossier and sit with ottoman-empire.

Counterparts: hatay-state (2 September 1938 to 23 July 1939, no Cliopatria row) was written by this batch (me-10-h); republic-of-cyprus and turkish-republic-of-northern-cyprus (Cliopatria rows exist: 1961-2024 and 1976-2024), syria (me-10). The Turkish military presence in northern Iraq and the Idlib zone (Operation Spring Shield, 27 February 2020) were not mapped: the pages give no boundary.

Not reached in the five-page budget: the Treaty of Kars (1921) and the eastern frontier, the Turkey-Iran frontier settlement (the Mount Ararat exchange of the 1930s) and the Turkish-Iraqi frontier of Mosul (decided in 1926), Imbros and Tenedos, the Dodecanese and Aegean islands (islands under one map cell), and the Turkish presence in northern Iraq. The Turkey page is long: the fetch returned its summary of the sentences asked for.

Gazetteer: Jarabulus, al-Bab, Afrin, Tell Abyad and Ras al-Ayn are not places in places.jsonl (circles around coordinates are used); 'Northern Cyprus' resolves as a country.
